intro: Convert PSI to MPa quickly for concrete compressive strength ratings, hydraulic cylinders, pressure vessels, and steel tensile testing. Each pound per square inch equals 0.006894757 megapascals (where 1 MPa equals 145.037738 psi and is identical to 1 N/mm²). Multiply your PSI reading by 0.00689476—or divide by 145.037738—for an exact PSI-to-megapascal conversion, or look up common engineering values below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia) & MPa vs. Msi
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between psi and MPa. Tire, HVAC, and hydraulic gauges usually read Gauge Pressure (psig) relative to ambient atmospheric pressure (~14.696 psi or 0.101325 MPa at sea level).
Do not confuse MPa (megapascal = 10⁶ Pa) with Msi or Mpsi (megapound per square inch = 10⁶ psi, used for elastic modulus of metals; 1 Msi = 6,894.76 MPa).

faqs.question: How many megapascals (MPa) are in 1 psi?
faqs.answer: 1 pound per square inch (psi) equals 0.00689476 megapascals (MPa). Conversely, 1 MPa equals approximately 145.03774 psi.

faqs.question: How do I convert PSI to MPa?
faqs.answer: Multiply PSI by 0.006894757 (or divide PSI by 145.037738). For example, 3,000 psi ÷ 145.037738 = 20.68427 MPa.

faqs.question: What is 4,000 psi concrete strength in MPa?
faqs.answer: 4,000 psi equals 27.57903 MPa (commonly rounded to 27.6 MPa, or paired with 28 MPa in metric structural concrete standards).

faqs.question: Is 1 MPa equal to 1 N/mm²?
faqs.answer: Yes. One megapascal equals 1,000,000 newtons per square meter (10⁶ N/m²), which simplifies identically to 1 newton per square millimeter (1 MPa = 1 N/mm²).
